messages:
Arin: Quick q — where should I put large nsys/perfetto bundles so folks can inspect? also what's the canonical naming + any scrub rules we should run before uploading?

Sophia: Use the perf S3 bucket: s3://inference-perf/traces — preferred. Put a small README alongside the trace with run metadata. Naming conv: <model>_<node>-<batch>-<seq>-<date>-<runid>.<ext>. Example: gptj_gpu1-b8-s1024-20260312-01.nsys.tar.gz

Dan: +1 to S3. If the file is >20GB, split with `tar` & `xz` or `pixz`. Also we prefer .tar.xz for dedupe. Example: `tar -I pixz -cf gptj-...tar.xz <trace-dir>` then `aws s3 cp --storage-class STANDARD_IA` to save cost.

Maria: What exactly to redact? The perf traces sometimes contain customer IDs in logs or mounted paths. My checklist: remove absolute paths, scrub ENV vars, and strip small text logs. For perfetto you can remove args by running `python perf_scrub.py --strip-args trace.pb` (we have a small script in infra/tools). For logs: `grep -vE "(customer|acct|org_id|api_key)" app.log > app.log.redacted`

Arin: Here's a sample upload flow I use:
```
# collect
nsys profile --output=nsys_run --sample=none --trace=on ...
# scrub
python infra/tools/perf_scrub.py nsys_run.qdstrace
# bundle
tar -I pixz -cf gptj_gpu1-b8-s1024-20260312-01.nsys.tar.xz nsys_run.* README.txt
# upload
aws s3 cp gptj_gpu1-...tar.xz s3://inference-perf/traces/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control
```
Add a `.redacted` suffix if you ran the scrub script, e.g. `...-01.nsys.redacted.tar.xz`.

perf-bot: (auto) Quick scan: 1) File size ok (<=100GB), 2) No obvious PII (paths matched none), 3) Missing README (reaction: :eyes:). Upload will be quarantined for 2h then visible to eng-runtime members.

Sophia: Also please annotate with a tiny manifest in the S3 object metadata: `x-amz-meta-run-id`, `x-amz-meta-model`, `x-amz-meta-commit`. It makes searching + retention much easier. See internal doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/perf-traces (internal only). Retention is 90 days by default.

Dan: For kernel-level debugging we like a short mapping file `kernels.csv` with columns: kernel_name, suspected_component, notes. If you can add perfetto user events around the interesting requests, that helps — e.g. `trace.add_user_event("kv-lookup-begin")` in the trace harness before the request.

Maria: Cool — I'll scrub with infra/tools/perf_scrub.py, add README + kernels.csv, and upload as `gptj_gpu1-b8-s1024-20260312-02.nsys.redacted.tar.xz`. Ping @Sophia and @Dan once it's there. :thumbsup:

Arin: Perfect, thanks. If anyone hits permission issues on the bucket ping @eng-infra. (reaction: :white_check_mark:)
